tasks.short: Check approved supplier and agency invoices, release them for the Rabobank payment batch, chase the ones that are stuck.

today.trigger: Invoices arrive in the AFAS inbox or by mail daily; the payment run is weekly.
steps: Open invoices waiting in the AFAS approval workflow and check coding, VAT and approver
Match staffing agency invoices to hours in the agency portals and to the flex order
Chase budget holders in Outlook and Teams for missing approvals
Build the payment batch in AFAS and export it to Rabobank
Check the batch total and any changed IBANs before release
drudgery: Comparing agency hours line by line with the invoice
Chasing approvers who sit in the warehouse without a laptop
Retyping PDF invoices that the scan did not read
today.time_sinks: Agency invoices with hour differences and approvals stuck with shift managers take most of the time.

lenses.faster: Invoices are read, coded and matched to orders and agency hours before anyone opens them; the accountant only sees the exceptions.
lenses.autonomous: A new invoice triggers matching and routing; matched invoices within tolerance go straight to the payment proposal.
lenses.ambitious: Every agency invoice is checked against every hour and CAO rate, not a sample, and overbilling is recovered.
lenses.joy: No more retyping or hour-by-hour comparisons; what is left is resolving real disputes with agencies.
lenses.options: The payment proposal comes with two or three cash scenarios (pay all, hold disputed, use early-payment discounts).
lenses.altitude: The accountant sets match tolerances, approval rules and IBAN-change checks and reviews the exception rate each month.
reach: Credit and collections cash planning for outgoing payments

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what to do with a disputed agency bill, and the final release of money out of the bank, stay with a person who carries the responsibility.
tasks.pattern_why: Several steps across AFAS, agency portals and the bank with many exceptions; a person must approve the payment batch before money leaves.

in_practice.trigger: Invoice lands in the AFAS inbox or a UBL file arrives; weekly payment run date.
steps: Read the invoice (UBL or PDF) and propose supplier, ledger, cost centre and VAT code
Match to purchase order or to agency hours and order, flag differences above tolerance
Route unmatched items to the right approver with the reason in plain text
Draft the payment batch and flag new or changed IBANs and duplicates
Accountant reviews exceptions and approves the batch in Rabobank
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant approves the batch, plus a second signer under the four-eyes rule, before release in Rabobank.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS invoice workflow history plus a match log per invoice

evidence.claim: AI can prepare finance entries from documents while people stay responsible for review.
Accountants using AI closed books faster across 79 small and mid-sized firms.
evidence.source: Choi and Xie via CFO Dive [S3]

evidence.claim: Dutch B2B e-invoicing is planned from 1 July 2030; a PDF is not an e-invoice, so OCR stays needed until then.
Matching agency hours to invoices is rules-based and can run without a model.

risks: Payment fraud through a changed IBAN that the agent accepts
Agency hour data in portals not exportable in a usable format
Approvers bypass the workflow by email, so matches miss context
research_questions: What share of invoices today match PO or hours within tolerance on the first try?
Can all three agency portals export hours by worker and week via API or CSV?
How many IBAN changes per quarter, and how are they verified now?

tasks.short: Prepare and check the monthly figures and reports from AFAS for accuracy and completeness before they go to the controller.

today.trigger: Month close and quarterly or annual reporting deadlines.
steps: Export the trial balance and sub-ledgers from AFAS to Excel
Compare balances with last month and budget and look for odd movements
Check that accruals, depreciation and intercompany between sites are booked
Write notes on differences for the controller
Fix errors and rerun the reports
drudgery: Rebuilding the same Excel checks every month
Scrolling transaction lists to explain a movement
today.time_sinks: Explaining unusual movements by digging through transactions across three sites.

lenses.faster: Standard completeness and analytic checks run automatically on the trial balance; the accountant starts from a list of flagged movements with draft explanations.
lenses.autonomous: When AFAS period data is final for a step, the check pack runs and posts results in the close channel.
lenses.ambitious: Every account on every site gets a documented review each month instead of only the large ones.
lenses.joy: No manual exports and copy-paste; the work becomes investigating the few things that look wrong.
lenses.options: For each flagged movement the tool offers likely causes ranked by evidence, not one guess.
lenses.altitude: The accountant owns the check library and thresholds and tunes them after each audit finding.
reach: Controller first review of the close pack

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a figure is materially wrong and what Dutch GAAP requires; benchmarks show models still miss multi-step judgement.
tasks.pattern_why: Checks are deterministic; turning transaction detail into a written explanation is an LLM step inside the close workflow with a tie-out gate.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS close step marked done for the period.
steps: Pull trial balance and sub-ledgers from AFAS
Run completeness and analytic checks against prior month and budget
Draft explanations for flagged movements with links to the transactions
Accountant reviews, corrects and signs off the pack
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant signs off each explanation; the controller signs the close pack.
in_practice.logs_to: Close pack on SharePoint with check results and sign-off

evidence.claim: On four month-end scenarios a model beat licensed CPAs on detail and file search, but the study left out judgement and communication.
On 160 US GAAP tasks the leading model meets 61.8% of criteria; multi-step reasoning is the main failure.

risks: Plausible but wrong explanations accepted without checking
Model adds an assumption that cannot be traced, so the workpaper cannot be rebuilt [S6]
research_questions: Which explanations in the last six close packs could have been drafted from AFAS data alone?
How often would the auditor have caught an error the checks missed?
Can AFAS GetConnectors deliver sub-ledger detail fast enough during close?

tasks.short: Reconcile bank, intercompany, AP, AR and balance sheet accounts and explain the differences.

today.trigger: Month end, and daily for bank.
steps: Download Rabobank statements and match them with AFAS bookings
Reconcile AP and AR sub-ledgers with the general ledger
Reconcile intercompany between Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo
Investigate open items and book corrections
Update the reconciliation files on SharePoint
drudgery: Hunting for small differences from rounding or timing
today.time_sinks: Intercompany and agency balances that do not agree and need mail back and forth.

lenses.faster: Matching runs on all items with rules; only unmatched items reach the accountant with suggested causes.
lenses.autonomous: Each CAMT.053 statement and each closed day triggers matching; reconciliations are always current, not only at month end.
lenses.ambitious: All balance sheet accounts reconciled monthly with evidence attached, which cuts audit adjustments.
lenses.joy: Ticking disappears; the accountant solves real breaks.
lenses.options: For an open item the tool proposes possible matches ranked by amount, date and reference.
lenses.altitude: The accountant writes and maintains the matching rules and tolerances and reviews the open-items trend.

tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a difference is an error, a timing issue or something to write off, and booking it.
tasks.pattern_why: Structured bank and ledger data with rules that can be written down and outputs that tie out.

in_practice.trigger: New CAMT.053 file from Rabobank, or ledger period closed.
steps: Import statements and ledger lines
Apply matching rules and tolerances
List unmatched items with suggested matches
Accountant resolves breaks and books corrections
Store reconciliation with evidence on SharePoint
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant approves any correcting entry and signs the month-end reconciliation.
in_practice.logs_to: Reconciliation log per account and period

evidence.claim: Cash checks from CAMT.053 suit deterministic software at high autonomy.
Faster close with AI in a field study.
evidence.source: Choi and Xie via CFO Dive [S3]

risks: Rules drift when AFAS ledger structure changes
research_questions: What share of bank lines does AFAS auto-matching already handle?
How many hours go into intercompany reconciliation per month?
How many audit adjustments last year came from reconciliations?

tasks.short: Check our books and AFAS setup for errors, weak controls and inefficient procedures.

today.trigger: Quarterly internal control review, audit preparation, or a problem found in close.
steps: Pull samples of transactions from AFAS
Check segregation of duties in AFAS roles
Test approvals and postings against procedure
Write findings and propose fixes
today.time_sinks: Sampling and documenting tests, which leaves little time to fix causes.

lenses.faster: Tests run over every transaction (duplicates, posting by approver, out-of-hours entries, IBAN changes) instead of samples.
lenses.autonomous: Control tests run weekly and alert on hits, not once a quarter.
lenses.ambitious: Continuous control monitoring that the external auditor can rely on, lowering audit fees and adjustments.
lenses.joy: No sampling by hand; time goes to fixing processes with colleagues.
lenses.options: For each weakness, several fixes with their cost and effect on workload.
lenses.altitude: The accountant designs the control test set and decides which hits matter.
reach: Payroll checks with the Payroll Specialist

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a process is effective, interviewing people, and agreeing fixes with the controller and teams.
tasks.pattern_why: Control tests over full transaction data are rules; an LLM step only writes the findings.

steps: Extract transactions and user roles from AFAS
Run the test library
Draft findings text for hits
Accountant reviews and agrees actions with owners
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant decides which hits are findings; controller approves process changes.

evidence.claim: Full-population tests for duplicates, segregation of duties and IBAN changes suit deterministic software at autonomy 4.
Interviews and judgement on effectiveness stay human.

risks: Too many false alerts so tests get ignored
Access to AFAS role data restricted
research_questions: Which control findings did the auditor raise in the last two years?
Can AFAS role and authorisation data be extracted automatically?
What false-positive rate is acceptable to the team?

tasks.short: Draft and book month-end corrections, accruals and reclassifications in AFAS.

steps: Collect accrual inputs (agency hours not yet invoiced, energy, rent)
Calculate amounts in Excel
Enter memorial entries in AFAS
Attach support and get controller review
drudgery: Recalculating the same accruals each month
today.time_sinks: Waiting for inputs such as uninvoiced agency hours.

lenses.faster: Recurring accruals are calculated and drafted with support; the accountant reviews instead of building.
lenses.autonomous: When agency hours and open POs are final, accrual drafts appear in AFAS waiting for approval.
lenses.ambitious: Accruals become precise enough that reversals next month barely move, cutting audit adjustments.
lenses.joy: No rebuilding of spreadsheets; time goes to unusual items.
lenses.options: For estimates, a low, central and high value with assumptions.
lenses.altitude: The accountant defines the accrual rules and tie-out checks.

tasks.human_edge: Estimates and judgement entries need a person who can defend them to the auditor.
tasks.pattern_why: Drafts from structured and semi-structured inputs inside the close workflow, with a tie-out gate before posting.

in_practice.trigger: Close calendar step and inputs complete.
steps: Pull inputs from AFAS and agency portals
Calculate recurring entries by rule; draft others with the LLM
Tie out to support and prior month
Accountant reviews and posts
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant posts; controller reviews entries above threshold.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS memorial journal with attached support

evidence.claim: Workday's agent prepares entries but does not post them; teams review.
Model scored well on month-end scenarios against CPAs.

research_questions: Which entries recur monthly with the same logic?
How large were last year's reversal differences?
Does the auditor accept system-drafted entries with attached support?

tasks.short: Guide the bookkeepers on filing, posting and sending financial records and documents.

steps: Answer bookkeeper questions in Teams
Assign close tasks and check they are done
Check documents are filed in AFAS and SharePoint
Coach on errors found
today.time_sinks: Repeated questions and follow-ups on close tasks.

lenses.faster: A procedure assistant answers routine questions from the SharePoint manuals.
lenses.autonomous: Close task status updates itself from AFAS and reminders go out automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Procedures written down properly for the first time, so new staff learn fast.
lenses.options: Several task plans for the close depending on absences.
lenses.altitude: The accountant maintains the procedures and the close plan instead of chasing.

tasks.human_edge: Leading people, setting priorities and coaching stay human.
tasks.pattern_why: The accountant leads people; AI supports with answers, status and drafts.

in_practice.trigger: Bookkeeper question or close task due.
steps: Assistant answers from procedures with source link
Task tracker reads AFAS status
Accountant reviews open items and coaches
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant decides priorities and owns procedure changes.

evidence.claim: Recordkeeping direction suits a copilot at autonomy 2.

research_questions: How many bookkeeper questions per week are routine?
Are current procedures complete enough to ground an assistant?

tasks.short: Maintain the AFAS chart of accounts and cost centres and fix entries booked to the wrong account.

today.trigger: New activity, cost centre or site change; misbookings found in close.
steps: Review requests for new accounts or cost centres
Set them up in AFAS
Find misposted entries
Reclassify them
today.time_sinks: Reclassifications in close caused by inconsistent coding.

lenses.faster: A classifier flags likely misposted lines and proposes the right account.
lenses.autonomous: Coding suggestions appear at entry time so errors do not reach close.
lenses.ambitious: A clean, documented chart with mapping to reporting and SBR filing.
lenses.options: Several chart designs for a new activity, with reporting impact.
lenses.altitude: The accountant owns coding rules and mapping.

tasks.human_edge: Designing the chart and deciding the right account in grey cases.
tasks.pattern_why: Free-text descriptions to account codes, checked against rules.

steps: Score entries for likely misposting
Propose account and reason
Accountant approves reclassifications
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant approves each reclassification and any chart change.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS memorial journal and chart change log

evidence.claim: Account assignment in close suits an LLM draft with tie-out gate at autonomy 3.
Large companies file via SBR from FY2025; AFAS cannot file this for them.

research_questions: How many reclassifications per close?
Is the chart mapped to the SBR taxonomy?

tasks.short: Improve and document our AFAS setup, Excel tools and reporting so finance processes run cleaner.

today.trigger: Process problems, new requirements such as e-invoicing, audit points.
steps: Identify a process weakness
Design a change in AFAS or Excel
Test and document it
Train colleagues
today.time_sinks: Documentation and testing take longer than the design.

lenses.faster: AI coding helps build scripts, Power BI measures and documentation in hours.
lenses.ambitious: Prepare properly for e-invoicing in 2030 and SBR filing.
lenses.options: Several designs with pros and cons.
lenses.altitude: The accountant becomes the owner of finance automation.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst AFAS work

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what to build and owning control impact.
tasks.pattern_why: Design work led by the person, AI helps build and document.

steps: Draft design options
Build with AI coding help
Test against sample data
Document and train
in_practice.human_gate: Controller approves changes to AFAS and controls.

evidence.claim: E-invoicing B2B from 1 July 2030 planned, not law yet.
Recordkeeping systems work suits copilot autonomy 2.

research_questions: Which processes need change for e-invoicing?
Who owns AFAS configuration today?

role.altitude: From posting, matching and checking entries to designing and owning the rules, tie-outs and control tests that check every entry, with the accountant reviewing exceptions and signing off.
reach: Bookkeeper invoice coding and bank matching
Controller close review and internal control framework
role.ceiling_note: Judgement entries, estimates, tax positions and conversations with the auditor and tax office stay human; no benchmark covers Dutch GAAP or VAT, and data access to agency portals limits automation.
skills_to_grow: Data extraction from AFAS (GetConnectors) and Power BI
Reviewing AI drafts for hidden assumptions
role.ambitious_version: Two accountants run a continuous close where reconciliations and control tests run daily over every transaction, the month closes in a few days with fewer audit adjustments, and the team is ready for e-invoicing before 2030.
